title: GPU headroom forecasting and soft-guard buckets for mixed inference workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As customer footprints diversify (short-chat, long-context chat, embedding bursts), our single global headroom heuristics lead to either over-provisioning of GPU memory (raising cost) or unexpected OOMs during tenant bursts. Current hard-threshold reserve policies cause brittle preemptions and complex failure modes when weights/KV/activations compete on heterogeneous hardware.

Goal: Build a predictive headroom forecasting and soft-guard bucket system that: (1) forecasts short-term GPU headroom requirements per device class and tenant cohort, (2) maintains lightweight soft buckets (elastic reserved cushions) that can be borrowed and repaid to tolerate microbursts, and (3) exposes safe, well-instrumented controls for rollout and fallbacks. The system should reduce OOM incidence by >60% in mixed workloads while limiting steady-state reserved memory uplift to <7% on average for production serving clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator produces 1m/5m/1h headroom forecasts and a confidence score for each GPU class
Controller implements soft-guard buckets that respect per-tenant quota and global safety corridor
End-to-end canary on 10% of fleet reduces OOM incidents in canary region by >=60% compared to baseline
Telemetry and dashboards show headroom utilization, borrow/repay events, and cost delta; no P95 latency regressions attributable to new control loop
Playbook for emergency rollback and manual override is documented and tested
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Telemetry and simulator - extend existing memory simulator (ENG-74890) to run sliding-window forecasts using seq-length-weighted request traces and KV occupancy decay models

Phase 2: Soft-guard algorithm - implement two-tier cushion: a fast transient bucket (timescale ~10-30s) and a slow safety corridor (timescale ~5-15m). Buckets are elastic and require repayment policies tied to token throughput budgets
Phase 3: Controller integration - integrate with runtime scheduler; controller peeks forecasts and adjusts per-tenant soft allocations using best-effort reservations and preemption budget tokens

Phase 4: Observability and rollout - add metrics (headroom_forecast_p95, bucket_borrow_count, bucket_repay_latency, bucket_violation_incidents) and dashboards; roll out via canary with automatic rollback when OOM rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds

Trade-offs: Conservative forecasting increases cost; aggressive repayment reduces burst resilience. We will start conservative with 95th percentile forecasts and tune toward cost as we collect borrow/repay telemetry

Safety: Hard OOM protection remains unchanged; soft-buckets must never disable hard safety checks. Security review not required for algorithmic changes, but config UI changes will be coordinated with console PM
comments: 2025-01-16 - Kickoff: Drafted simulator requirements. Agreed to model KV decay as exponential with per-model half-life parameter. Action: Maya to run traces from last 30 days.

2025-01-22 - Spike results: Prototype simulator suggests 5-9% memory uplift for 95th percentile headroom using current traffic patterns. Noted that long-context chat tenants dominate headroom variance. Action: run per-tenant cohort analysis.

2025-01-28 - Design review: PM and runtime leads prefer two-tier soft-bucket approach to isolate microburst handling from longer-term safety corridor. Concern: repayment fairness across tenants. Decision: implement proportional repayment based on recent token budget and tenant priority labels.

2025-01-30 - Implementation update: Simulator integrated into nightly bench harness. Synthetic mixed footprints test shows OOM reduction from 0.9/day to 0.2/day in 1h window when buckets allowed. Need more real-trace validation.

2025-02-01 - PR feedback (Arjun): Add metric for bucket starvation events and expose bucket size proposals in the allocation API. Also add unit tests that simulate repeated borrow and repay cycles to verify no memory leakage.

2025-02-02 - Ops note: Plan canary on a single AZ with 12 GPUs next week. Runbook drafted: if bucket_borrow_rate > 30/min and OOM > baseline for 30m, rollback controller and re-enable conservative reservations. Assigned to oncall: Lena Rodriguez.
